title: Grade 6 Order of Operations
seo_title: Grade 6 Order of Operations Worksheets: Free BEDMAS Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Order of operations with whole numbers
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on the order of operations, matched to the BC curriculum: × and ÷ before + and −, left to right, brackets, multiplication and division facts, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Brackets first, then ÷ and × from left to right, then + and − from left to right.
body_html:
Why the order matters

An expression with more than one operation can give different answers if people work in a different order. So everyone uses the same order of operations.

StepDo thisExample
1Brackets(25 + 15) × 3 = 40 × 3 = 120
2÷ and ×, as equals, from left to right12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 6 × 3 = 18
3+ and −, as equals, from left to right20 − 8 + 3 = 12 + 3 = 15

Many Canadian classrooms remember the order as BEDMAS: Brackets, Exponents, Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction. Grade 6 expressions have no exponents, so you can skip the E for now.

Multiply before you add

Evaluate 7 + 6 × 8.

7 + 6 × 8 = 7 + 48 = 55. Not 104: that adds first.

Answer: 55

Same rank: work from left to right

÷ and × have the same rank, so do whichever comes first from the left. The same is true for + and −. Division does not always come before multiplication.

Brackets first

Brackets change the order. Work out what is inside the brackets before anything else.

Facts make it quick

Most steps use multiplication and division facts to 100. Know them well and each step takes a moment.

Two facts, then add

Evaluate 56 ÷ 8 + 9 × 6.

56 ÷ 8 + 9 × 6 = 7 + 9 × 6 = 7 + 54 = 61. The facts are 56 ÷ 8 = 7 and 9 × 6 = 54.

Answer: 61

Word problems as one expression

Write the whole problem as one expression, then use the order of operations. Use brackets when a sum or difference must be found before you multiply or divide.

Change from $50

Arjun buys 4 packs of hockey cards at $6 each and pays with a $50 bill. How much change does he get?

One expression: 50 − 4 × 6 = 50 − 24 = 26.

Answer: $26

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
2 + 3 × 4 = 5 × 4 = 20Multiply first: 2 + 12 = 14
12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 12 ÷ 6 = 2÷ and × are equals: left to right, 6 × 3 = 18
20 − 8 + 3 = 20 − 11 = 9+ and − are equals: left to right, 12 + 3 = 15
(8 + 4) × 3 = 8 + 12 = 20Brackets first: 12 × 3 = 36
50 − 4 × 6 = 46 × 6 = 276Multiply first: 50 − 24 = 26

faq.q: What is the order of operations in Grade 6 math?
faq.a: Work out brackets first, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. For example, 2 + 3 × 4 = 2 + 12 = 14, not 20.

BEDMAS stands for Brackets, Exponents, Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction. Division and multiplication are equals, and so are addition and subtraction, so 12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 18. Grade 6 work has no exponents yet.

faq.q: Is BEDMAS the same as PEMDAS and BODMAS?
faq.a: Yes. PEMDAS (used in the US) and BODMAS (used in the UK) give the same order with different words. In all of them, × and ÷ have the same rank and so do + and −.

faq.q: Where is order of operations in the BC Grade 6 math curriculum?
faq.a: It is in the Grade 6 Computational fluency content: order of operations with whole numbers. Students also build fluency with multiplication and division facts to 100, which they use at every step.

What number goes in the box?

items.e: Take away the 6 first: 69 − 6 = 63. Then 7 × 9 = 63, so the number is 9. Not 63: that stops before dividing by 7. Not 10: 7 × 10 + 6 = 76. Not 75: that adds the 6 instead of taking it away.

items.q: A SkyTrain has 4 cars with 30 seats in each car. There are 25 people sitting down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: One expression: 4 × 30 − 25. 4 × 30 − 25 = 120 − 25 = 95, so 95 seats. Not 20 seats: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 145 seats: that uses the wrong sign. Not 9 seats: that adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Arjun buys 4 packs of hockey cards at $6 each. He pays with a $50 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: One expression: 50 − 4 × 6. 50 − 4 × 6 = 50 − 24 = 26, so $26. Not $276: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not $44: that pays for only one pack. Not $24: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A class orders 8 pizzas. Each pizza is cut into 8 slices. Each of the 30 students eats 2 slices. How many slices are left?
items.e: One expression: 8 × 8 − 30 × 2. 8 × 8 − 30 × 2 = 64 − 30 × 2 = 64 − 60 = 4, so 4 slices. Not 68 slices: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 34 slices: that gives each student only 1 slice. Not 64 slices: that stops one step too early.

items.q: Two soccer teams, with 11 and 13 players, share 72 orange slices equally. How many slices does each player get?
items.e: One expression: 72 ÷ (11 + 13). 72 ÷ (11 + 13) = 72 ÷ 24 = 3, so 3 slices. Not 48 slices: that subtracts instead of dividing. Not 36 slices: that shares between the 2 teams, not between the players. Not 24 slices: that is the number of players, not slices.

items.q: In a class math game, a correct answer scores 5 points and a bonus question scores 10 points. Nadia gets 9 correct answers and 3 bonus questions. What is her score?
items.e: One expression: 9 × 5 + 3 × 10. 9 × 5 + 3 × 10 = 45 + 3 × 10 = 45 + 30 = 75, so 75 points. Not 480 points: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 720 points: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 45 points: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A school raises $1240 at its Terry Fox Run. Then 6 classes each raise another $45 at a bake sale. How much does the school raise in all?
items.e: One expression: 1240 + 6 × 45. 1240 + 6 × 45 = 1240 + 270 = 1510, so $1510. Not $56 070: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not $1285: that counts only one class. Not $270: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A Grade 6 class of 27 students visits the Vancouver Aquarium. Each ticket costs $14, and the bus costs $250. What is the total cost?
items.e: One expression: 27 × 14 + 250. 27 × 14 + 250 = 378 + 250 = 628, so $628. Not $7128: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not $291: that adds all the numbers. Not $378: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A lacrosse team has 3 cases of 24 water bottles. The coaches keep 8 bottles. The 16 players share the rest equally. How many bottles does each player get?
items.e: One expression: (3 × 24 − 8) ÷ 16. (3 × 24 − 8) ÷ 16 = (72 − 8) ÷ 16 = 64 ÷ 16 = 4, so 4 bottles. Not 64 bottles: that forgets to share among the players. Not 5 bottles: that adds the coaches’ bottles instead of taking them away. Not 72 bottles: that forgets the coaches and the sharing.

items.q: Liam picks 6 baskets of 12 peaches in the Okanagan. He packs them in bags of 8. How many bags does he fill?
items.e: One expression: 6 × 12 ÷ 8. 6 × 12 ÷ 8 = 72 ÷ 8 = 9, so 9 bags. Not 72 bags: that forgets to put the peaches in bags. Not 576 bags: that multiplies by 8 instead of dividing. Not 64 bags: that subtracts 8 instead of dividing.

items.q: Mateo saves $15 a week for 8 weeks. Then he spends $48 on soccer cleats and $12 on socks. How much money does he have left?
items.e: One expression: 15 × 8 − 48 − 12. 15 × 8 − 48 − 12 = 120 − 48 − 12 = 72 − 12 = 60, so $60. Not $84: that comes from working from right to left. Not $180: that adds the costs instead of subtracting them. Not $72: that stops one step too early.

items.q: Ethan has 56 hockey cards. He keeps 8 and shares the rest equally among 6 friends. Which expression gives each friend’s share?
items.e: (56 − 8) ÷ 6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8. So each friend gets 8 cards. Brackets are needed so you subtract before you divide.

items.q: A day pass at a small ski hill near Kelowna costs $65 for an adult and $38 for a youth. How much do 2 adults and 3 youths pay?
items.e: One expression: 2 × 65 + 3 × 38. 2 × 65 + 3 × 38 = 130 + 3 × 38 = 130 + 114 = 244, so $244. Not $5054: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not $103: that pays for only one adult and one youth. Not $515: that pays both prices for every person.

items.q: A family of 5 takes BC Ferries to Vancouver Island. The fare is $68 for the car and $19 for each person. What is the total fare?
items.e: One expression: 68 + 5 × 19. 68 + 5 × 19 = 68 + 95 = 163, so $163. Not $1387: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not $435: that charges the car fare 5 times. Not $87: that counts only one person.

items.q: Ava buys 3 notebooks at $4 each and a binder for $7. Which expression gives the total cost?
items.e: 3 × 4 + 7 = 12 + 7 = 19. So the total is $19. 3 × (4 + 7) would mean 3 binders. The other two multiply the wrong numbers.

items.q: Two classes, with 26 and 28 students, make teams of 6 for a field day. Which expression gives the number of teams?
items.e: (26 + 28) ÷ 6 = 54 ÷ 6 = 9. So there are 9 teams. Brackets are needed: without them you would divide only the 28 by 6.

items.q: Hana has $40. She buys 3 movie tickets at $11 each. Which expression gives the money she has left?
items.e: 40 − 3 × 11 = 40 − 33 = 7. So she has $7 left. (40 − 3) × 11 subtracts before multiplying. 3 × 11 − 40 subtracts in the wrong order.

items.q: A class plants 6 rows of 9 cedar seedlings near the Fraser River. Later, 7 seedlings do not survive. How many seedlings are left?
items.e: One expression: 6 × 9 − 7. 6 × 9 − 7 = 54 − 7 = 47, so 47 seedlings. Not 12 seedlings: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 8 seedlings: that adds instead of multiplying. Not 61 seedlings: that uses the wrong sign.

items.q: Owen bikes 8 km to Stanley Park and 8 km back home. In the park he rides a 9 km loop on the seawall. How far does he bike in all?
items.e: One expression: 2 × 8 + 9. 2 × 8 + 9 = 16 + 9 = 25, so 25 km. Not 34 km: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 17 km: that forgets the ride back home. Not 16 km: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A whale-watching boat in Victoria takes 4 groups of 9 students and 6 teachers. How many people from the school are on the boat?
items.e: One expression: 4 × 9 + 6. 4 × 9 + 6 = 36 + 6 = 42, so 42 people. Not 60 people: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 19 people: that adds all the numbers. Not 36 people: that stops one step too early.

items.q: Zara earns $8 an hour for 5 hours of babysitting. She also gets a $10 tip. Which expression gives the money she earns?
items.e: 8 × 5 + 10 = 40 + 10 = 50. So she earns $50. 8 × (5 + 10) would pay her for 15 hours. The other two multiply the wrong numbers.
